newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Abiola's family writes Nigeria's Abacha for access.
newsitem.headline: Abiola's family writes Nigeria's Abacha for access.

text.p: The family of presidential claimant Moshood Abiola has asked military ruler General Sani Abacha for permisson to see the jailed politician because of concern about his health.
In a letter to Abacha signed by Mariam, one of Abiola's wives, the family said they had read of Abiola's "deteriorating health". Copies of the letter were distributed to the media on Sunday.
The opposition Tell magazine said last week that Abiola might soon die. Tell did not say how it got the information.
"As we have been denied access to him for 20 months, granting the request to see the detained politician will disabuse our minds of the purported danger to his health and life," the letter said.

Abiola, a multi-millionaire businessman, is widely believed to have won an annulled 1993 presidential election. He has been held since 1994 when he proclaimed himself president in defiance of the army.
He has not been seen in public since August 1994 when he last appeared in court on charges of treason.

Annulment of the 1993 poll plunged Africa's most populous nation into crisis. Abacha, who seized power in the chaos after the annulment, says he will hand power to a democratically-elected president in October 1998.
Critics of the Abacha government have dismissed the transition programme, saying it is too slow and that he intends to succeed himself.
